title: [review] project-LICHEN-2auf.44.11.1.1: EdhocInitiator/EdhocResponder lost struct-level ZeroizeOnDrop
description:
The `#[derive(Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop)]` was removed from both `EdhocInitiator` (line ~894) and `EdhocResponder` (line ~1257). While `SigningKey` and `StaticSecret` implement `ZeroizeOnDrop` internally, the composite `state` field (`InitiatorState`/`ResponderState`) contains derived key material (`prk_2e`, `prk_3e2m`, `prk_4e3m` — 96 bytes of HKDF-derived secrets) that will not be zeroized when the parent struct is dropped.

The inner `InitiatorState` and `ResponderState` structs retain their own `#[derive(Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop)]`, but that only triggers when the state field itself is dropped — not when the parent struct is dropped. The `poison()` methods exist on both structs but are only called on explicit error paths, not on drop.

A dropped `EdhocInitiator` after a successful handshake would leave 96 bytes of PRK material recoverable in memory.

Fix: restore `#[derive(Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop)]` on both structs, or implement explicit `Drop` that calls `zeroize()`.
